paragraphs: Here's what I love about this one, friend. Abimelech, a king with an army, looks at Abraham and says, "God is with you in all that you do." (Genesis 21:22) A king noticed it. That tells me when God is with you, people see it, even people who don't share your faith. Nobody had to hand Abraham a trophy for it either.

Now look at how Abraham handles a problem. His well got seized, and he doesn't stew in silence or start a feud. He brings it straight to the king, and the king says, "You did not tell me, so I have not heard about it until today." (Genesis 21:26) Friend, how many of us have been sitting on a hurt that the other person doesn't even know about? Abraham talks it out, makes a covenant, and the well is settled for good.

And after the dust settles, Abraham doesn't run off to celebrate. He plants a tamarisk tree, and there he "called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God." (Genesis 21:33) He's setting down roots and worshiping the God who stays the same, in a land where he's a guest and "for a long time" (Genesis 21:34). So settle things honestly, speak up kindly, and then call on the Eternal God, baker. That's a recipe I'd stamp on any day of the week. The story isn't over, either.
